subject: Proposed Real Estate Transfer Fee
overview: City Councilors Kit Collins and Matt Leming discussed a proposed 0.5% to 2% fee on high-value real estate transactions to fund the city's Affordable Housing Trust. The conversation detailed the legislative path via a Home Rule petition and how the revenue would support housing production and tenant preservation.

items.title: Definition and Purpose of the Transfer Fee
items.summary: Matt Leming defined the proposed policy as a small percentage fee on luxury real estate sales to provide a dedicated revenue stream for the Affordable Housing Trust.

items.title: Legislative Process for Home Rule Petitions
items.summary: Kit Collins explained that Medford must petition the state for special permission to enact the fee, though proposed state legislation could eventually allow the city to opt in by default.

items.title: Current Legislative Status
items.summary: The City Council referred the resolution to develop a Home Rule petition to the Planning and Permitting Committee following a March 12th meeting.

items.title: Affordable Housing Deficit and Legal Requirements
items.summary: Councilors noted that Medford remains approximately 671 units short of the state-mandated 10% affordability threshold and highlighted the role of the recently created Affordable Housing Trust.

items.title: Integration with Broader Housing Tools
items.summary: The transfer fee was characterized as one tool among several, including zoning recodification and linkage fees, intended to address the regional housing crisis.

items.title: Addressing Resident Displacement
items.summary: The discussion highlighted recent displacements at 208 Main Street and Brooks Park Apartments as evidence of the need for local funds to intervene when naturally occurring affordable housing is sold for redevelopment.

items.title: Public Engagement and Next Steps
items.summary: Councilors encouraged residents to participate via committee meetings, public comment, and direct correspondence as the petition moves through the local and state legislative processes.
